key_insight: CB-COMIL explains melanoma immunotherapy-response predictions through four supervised concepts, but those concepts are not interchangeable with measured biology.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more interpretable immunotherapy-response research, but clinical utility for treatment selection remains unproven.
method: Analyzes multiplex immunofluorescence whole-slide images using a concept bottleneck model.
Routes predictions through immune:tumour ratio, CD8/SOX10 balance, CD68 relative signal and PD-L1 evasion index.
Decomposes each prediction exactly into contributions from the four concepts.
evidence_signal: Developed on 211 slides and tested on 42 independently acquired slides, CB-COMIL achieved macro-F1 0.69 versus 0.67 for an opaque comparator (difference 0.020; 95% CI −0.103 to 0.144).
watch_item: In 41 slides with complete measurements, replacing learned concepts with measured counterparts reduced macro-F1 from 0.68 to 0.48 despite correlations of 0.61–0.76, cautioning against interpreting learned concepts as direct biological measurements.
paper_title: CB-COMIL: interpretable prediction of melanoma immunotherapyresponse from multiplex immunofluorescence whole-slide images
